claim: Foot Locker U.K. Ltd's first accounts after the deal (FY to 31 Dec 2024, signed 24 Nov 2025) say the UK business opened 2 stores and closed 3 in 2025 (one closure was a relocation), and for 2026 plans 1 opening with 3 closures approved. The FY2022 and FY2023 accounts mentioned only openings, expansions or refits, so closures appear in the UK plan for the first time.
data_point: UK 2025: +2 / -3 (net -1, one closure a relocation), 12 store modifications. 2026 plan: +1 / -3 approved (net -2). FY2022 accounts (signed 23 Nov 2023): 'one store opening, one store expansion and remodeling in 2023'. FY2023 accounts (signed 12 Dec 2024): 'one new store opening and 7 minor stores modification in 2024'.
source_name: Companies House: Foot Locker UK Limited (02568406) annual report & consolidated FS, FY ended 31 Dec 2024 (AA filed 01 Dec 2025), Strategic report, Outlook and future developments, p.3
original_quote: The entity has opened 2 stores and closed 3 stores in 2025, one of which for relocation, with 12 stores modification. For 2026 1 new opening is planned and 3 closures approved.
verifier_note: Independently downloaded the PDF (md5 matches the scraper's copy) and read p.3 (page image): quote is verbatim, signed by E J Amperse and G S Lönell on 24 Nov 2025. Also read the FY2023 and FY2022 outlook pages; the earlier wording is as stated. Caveats: the scale is small (net -2 in 2026 against a UK estate of a few dozen stores). The same paragraph says 'No significant changes are expected in the number of employees'. The '2025' figures are year-to-date at signing (Nov 2025). Not in the baseline or the brief, which has only Europe-wide counts.

claim: UK selling space fell 8.6% in FL fiscal 2024 (285,762 vs 312,640 sq ft). Non-cancellable UK land-and-building lease commitments fell 22% to GBP58.8m, and only GBP6.4m falls due after more than 5 years. The lease tail is short, so cutting the UK estate would be relatively cheap.
data_point: Leases (GBP000) 2024 vs 2023: <1yr 15,740 vs 16,919; 1-5yrs 36,607 vs 49,638; >5yrs 6,429 vs 8,439; total 58,776 vs 74,996 (-21.6%). 89% of commitments fall due within 5 years. Loss on retirement of assets GBP846k (2023: 286k). Guarantees of lease commitments for stores of fellow Foot Locker Europe B.V. group companies: GBP2,138k (2023: 3,665k).
source_name: Foot Locker UK Ltd FY2024 accounts: Directors' report SECR table (p.5), Note 2, Note 15 Operating leases, Note 16 Contingent liability
original_quote: Total Square Footage 285,762 [2024] 312,640 [2023]; Non-cancellable operating leases ... Less than one year 15,740; Between one and five years 36,607; More than five years 6,429; 58,776 (2023: 74,996)
verifier_note: All figures checked on the page images of the filed PDF. Caveats: (1) the square footage comes from the SECR energy table, covers FL fiscal 2024 (ended 1 Feb 2025) and may include non-store sites; (2) these are pre-deal figures; (3) 'cheap exit' is the scraper's inference, and lease commitments exclude dilapidations and works-council or redundancy costs. Not in the baseline.

claim: The UK business is a thin-margin limited-risk distributor run from the Netherlands. Retail risk is borne by Foot Locker Europe B.V. under a Distribution and Service Agreement, and a transfer-pricing agreement sets the operating profit the UK group can earn. FY2024 turnover was GBP175.0m at a 4.2% gross margin, with 1,109 average employees.
data_point: Turnover GBP174,991k (2023: 163,435k, +7.1%); gross profit 7,329k (4.2%; 2023: 3.5%); operating profit 4,872k; PBT 4,661k; average employees 1,109 (1,082 sales, 27 admin; 2023: 1,036). Immediate parent Foot Locker Europe B.V. (NL); sole subsidiary Freedom Sportsline Ltd.
source_name: Foot Locker UK Ltd FY2024 accounts: Strategic report (p.1), Going concern (p.8), Notes 7 and 17
original_quote: These risks are borne by Foot Locker Europe B.V. (under a Distribution and Service Agreement) ... subject to a transfer pricing agreement which specifies the operating profit that Foot Locker UK Limited group is able to generate
verifier_note: Turnover, gross profit, margin, operating profit, PBT, headcount, the risk/DSA sentence and the transfer-pricing sentence were all read on the filed page images. Net assets (GBP39.4m) and payroll (GBP19.7m) were not re-checked. Implication (inference): UK P&L is set by transfer pricing, so the economics of any UK sale or licence run through the Dutch principal. Not in the baseline.

claim: The UK entities' board was reshuffled after the deal. Matthew Barnes and Benjamin Boylan were appointed to the Foot Locker U.K. board on 13 Mar 2026, and Boylan was removed on 4 Jun 2026. Neil Carter joined on 19 Jun 2026. Company secretary Gözde Sen Lönell left on 17 Jun 2026. Reid Sigal, SVP and COO of FL EMEA (over Real Estate, Construction & Facilities, Supply Chain and Strategy) and 13 years at DICK'S, became secretary of both UK entities on 10 Jul 2026.
data_point: Current FL UK officers: directors E.J. Amperse (since 14 Nov 2023), M.C. Barnes (13 Mar 2026), N.G. Carter (19 Jun 2026); secretary R.J. Sigal (10 Jul 2026). Freedom Sportsline: directors Amperse and Barnes, secretary Sigal (10 Jul 2026). Filings: AP01 x2 on 01 Apr 2026, TM01 on 18 Jun 2026, TM02/AP03 on 22 Jul 2026, AP01 Carter on 07 Aug 2026.
source_name: Companies House officers and filing history for 02568406 and 01779106; Foot Locker IR bio of Reid Sigal (footlocker-inc.gcs-web.com/executive-leadership/reid-sigal)
original_quote: Appointment of Reid Joshua Sigal as a secretary on 10 July 2026; Termination of appointment of Benjamin James Boylan as a director on 4 June 2026; Appointment of Neil Geoffrey Carter as a director on 19 June 2026
verifier_note: CH officers and filing-history pages fetched live: all dates match, and Freedom Sportsline also lists Sigal as secretary from 10 Jul 2026. The Sigal bio was fetched live: 'SVP, Chief Operating Officer, Foot Locker EMEA ... oversees EMEA's PAR, Real Estate, Construction & Facilities, Supply Chain and Strategy teams ... spent 13 years at DICK'S'. claim: Tomas Petersson, Foot Locker's SVP and GM for EMEA, resigned as a director of Foot Locker U.K. on 1 Aug 2025, five weeks before DKS closed the deal. Genesco later named him President of schuh, a UK sneaker competitor (World Footwear, 30 Jul 2026).
data_point: CH TM01 filed 07 Aug 2025, effective 1 Aug 2025. The FY2024 accounts list 'T.C. Petersson (resigned August 1st, 2025)'. Genesco/World Footwear: he will work with Colin Temple over the coming months on the transition.
source_name: Companies House TM01 for 02568406; FY2024 accounts directors list (p.6); World Footwear 2026-07-30 (Genesco release)
original_quote: Termination of appointment of Tomas Conny Petersson as a director on 1 August 2025
verifier_note: CH filing history and the accounts' directors list confirm the 1 Aug 2025 resignation. World Footwear (30 Jul 2026) confirms the schuh presidency and his former role as 'Senior Vice President and General Manager for the EMEA region'. The quote 'leading the company's largest international business' comes from the Genesco release and was not re-fetched. 'EMEA had no GM until Barnes' is inference. The baseline (BL07) has Petersson only as SVP EMEA at the 2023 Investor Day, not his exit. HIGH DUPLICATE RISK: the Petersson-to-schuh exit is also in raw files A_w1_company-side-new, A_w1_people-jobs and B_w1 dach/benelux/italy-iberia. The UK-specific novelty is the 1 Aug 2025 CH resignation date.

Foot Locker Retail Ireland Ltd (CRO 391370) filed B10 director/secretary-change forms effective 11 Mar 2026 (received 9 Apr) and 23 Jul 2026 (received 19 Aug). Its parent, FL Finance (Europe) Ltd (CRO 391464, a holding company listed in DKS's Exhibit 21), filed B10s effective 7 Oct 2025 and 1 Oct 2026 (received 5 Oct 2026).
data_point: Both companies have status NORMAL and are registered at 49 Lower O'Connell St, Dublin 1. FL Retail Ireland's shareholder is FL Finance (Europe) Ltd. FL Finance (Europe)'s single director has been a director of 19 other Irish companies, 17 now closed. FY2024 financial statement (21 pp) filed with the annual return made up to 23 Sep 2025 (received 2 Oct 2025). Who joined or left is not visible without buying the paid documents.

claim: The Irish arm is small (7 stores in Dublin and Limerick) and returned to profit in FY2024, with turnover up about EUR5m. FY2022 figures were sales EUR11.54m, a pre-tax loss of EUR115k and 23 staff.
data_point: FY2022: revenue EUR11.54m (+16% from 9.95m), PBT -EUR115k (2021: +161k), 23 employees, operating lease cost EUR1.93m (2021: 2.73m), equity EUR7.6m. FY2024: returned to profit, turnover +EUR5m (exact figures paywalled).
source_name: Business Post (Emma Hanrahan, 2025-10-04) headline; BreakingNews.ie (Gordon Deegan, 2023-12-07)
original_quote: Footlocker's Irish arm returns to profit as turnover increases by €5m
verifier_note: Business Post page fetched: headline, byline Emma Hanrahan and date 4 Oct 2025 confirmed; the body is paywalled. BreakingNews.ie fetched: 7 stores (O'Connell St, Grafton St, Blanchardstown, The Square, Ilac, Pavilions, Limerick), EUR11.54m, -EUR115k, 23 staff, EUR1.93m leases and EUR7.6m equity all confirmed. Pre-deal and immaterial to the Europe thesis. Not in the baseline.

claim: There is no sign of distress or a sale vehicle in the UK registry. Dick's Sporting Goods, Inc. was notified as the 75%+ person with significant control of FL UK from 8 Sep 2025, replacing Foot Locker, Inc. FL UK has 0 charges, and Freedom Sportsline has only legacy rent-deposit charges. Name and registered office are unchanged, and FY2025 UK accounts are due by 31 Dec 2026.
data_point: PSC02/PSC07/PSC05 filed 02 Oct 2025. FL UK: 0 charges. Freedom Sportsline: 3 charges (2 outstanding: NatWest GBP1.56m deposit 2012; Cheshire CC rent deposit GBP44,943.75 1998; Barclays debenture 1984, satisfied 2002). Registered office c/o Womble Bond Dickinson, 4 More London Riverside. CS01 12 Dec 2025 'no updates'. Next accounts (to 31 Dec 2025) due 31 Dec 2026; next confirmation statement due 26 Dec 2026.
